Async context switching for racesan hooks and stepwise execution.

# Purpose
`fd_racesan_async.c` implements an asynchronous wrapper around a race-sanitizer target function by using `ucontext` stack switching. It creates a separate execution context for `async->fn`, runs that function on its own stack, and returns control to the caller each time the race-sanitizer hook fires. The helper [`fd_racesan_async_hook`](<#fd_racesan_async_hook>) records the hook name hash, exits the race-sanitizer scope, and yields back to the caller through [`fd_racesan_async_yield`](<#fd_racesan_async_yield>). The [`fd_racesan_async_target`](<#fd_racesan_async_target>) function sets up the race-sanitizer state, installs the hook callback, runs the target function, marks the async task as done, and then yields one last time.

The public functions in the file manage the life cycle and step control for the async runner. [`fd_racesan_async_new`](<#fd_racesan_async_new>) initializes the async object, sets up its stack, and prepares the context with `makecontext`. [`fd_racesan_async_step`](<#fd_racesan_async_step>) switches into the async context and returns after the target yields or finishes. [`fd_racesan_async_hook_name_eq`](<#fd_racesan_async_hook_name_eq>) compares the last hook name against a string by hashing the name, and [`fd_racesan_async_reset`](<#fd_racesan_async_reset>) rebuilds the context so the async task can run again.
